title: [Advanced Paste][PowerDisplay] Move from own IPC implementation to the one from PowerToys.interop
author: noraa-junker
summary: The unchanged current upstream head still needs three coordinated IPC fixes: retain and dispose the managed endpoints while ordering PowerDisplay startup safely, preserve commands while a child pipe is starting, and release IPC/process resources when disabling after a child has exited. The review-fix candidate rebuilt successfully and the targeted delayed-peer regression passed.

proposed_comments.title: Retain and dispose the managed IPC endpoints
proposed_comments.body:
### Retain and dispose the managed IPC endpoints

**Severity:** `high`

Both applications still keep `TwoWayPipeMessageIPCManaged` only in a local variable, so the wrapper can be collected after startup and neither shutdown path can call `Dispose()`, which is what deletes the native IPC object. Retain the endpoint as an application field and dispose it during the existing shutdown path. In PowerDisplay, create and assign the main window before starting IPC so an immediately delivered first command cannot be discarded while `_mainWindow` is still null.

confidence.rationale: The current code uses local wrappers, the WinRT Close implementation deletes the native pointer, and PowerDisplay's callback explicitly no-ops while _mainWindow is null.

proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: This concern requires coordinated changes across multiple current-diff regions or files, so it cannot be safely expressed as one apply-ready inline suggestion.

proposed_comments.title: Do not drop commands while the child pipe is starting
proposed_comments.body:
### Do not drop commands while the child pipe is starting

**Severity:** `high`

The old implementation did not return until the child connected, but the shared sender removes a queued message and returns when `CreateFile` reports `ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND`. A hotkey or profile command issued during child startup can therefore be lost. Retain and retry that queued message until the peer pipe appears or IPC is ended, and add a deterministic regression test that waits until the missing-pipe attempt has occurred before creating the peer.

confidence.rationale: The shared send loop returns on ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND after the queue has already popped the message; a deterministic native test reproduces and verifies the corrected behavior.

proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: This concern requires coordinated changes across multiple current-diff regions or files, so it cannot be safely expressed as one apply-ready inline suggestion.

proposed_comments.title: Release IPC when disabling an already-stopped child
proposed_comments.body:
### Release IPC when disabling an already-stopped child

**Severity:** `medium`

If either child exits before its module is disabled, `refresh()` sees both the desired and observed running states as false and returns before cleanup. That leaves the signaled process handle and the shared IPC queue workers retained while the disabled module remains loaded. Close the stale process handle and reset the IPC endpoint before taking this early-return path in both process managers.

confidence.rationale: The early equality return precedes every handle and IPC reset, and the stopped process handle remains nonzero even though is_process_running() is false.

proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: This concern requires coordinated changes across multiple current-diff regions or files, so it cannot be safely expressed as one apply-ready inline suggestion.

judgment.rationale: The current managed wrappers are local and not disposed, PowerDisplay can accept callbacks before its window exists, the shared sender can drop a command before the child pipe exists, and the process managers can retain stale handles and IPC workers after a child exits.
evidence: Advanced Paste and PowerDisplay create TwoWayPipeMessageIPCManaged as local variables while Dispose/Close is the native deletion path.
PowerDisplay starts IPC before assigning its main window, and its callback discards work while that window is null.
The shared send loop can dequeue a message and return on ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND before the child pipe server is ready.
Both process managers can return on the disabled/already-stopped path before releasing the signaled process handle and IPC endpoint.
